sanskrit: asmāṃs tu punar āsādya labdhalakṣāḥ prahāriṇaḥ śarāsanāni dhunvānāḥ siṃhanādān pracukruśuḥ
english: But falling upon us once more, those striking warriors, sure of their aim, brandished their bows and raised great lion-roars.

sanskrit: tato hatam abhiprekṣya madrarājabalaṃ mahat madrarājaṃ ca samare dṛṣṭvā śūraṃ nipātitam duryodhanabalaṃ sarvaṃ punar āsīt parāṅmukham
english: Then, beholding the great host of the king of the Madras struck down, and seeing the valiant king of the Madras laid low in battle, the whole army of Duryodhana once again turned its face away.

sanskrit: vadhyamānaṃ mahārāja pāṇḍavair jitakāśibhiḥ diśo bheje 'tha saṃbhrāntaṃ trāsitaṃ dṛḍhadhanvibhiḥ
english: Cut down, O great king, by the Pāṇḍavas flushed with victory, terrified and bewildered, it scattered to all directions, driven in panic by those firm-bowed warriors.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pātite yudhi durdharṣe madrarāje mahārathe tāvakās tava putrāś ca prāyaśo vimukhābhavan
english: Saṃjaya said: When the unassailable king of the Madras, that great chariot-warrior, was felled in battle, your men and your sons for the most part turned their backs.

sanskrit: vaṇijo nāvi bhinnāyāṃ yathāgādhe 'plave 'rṇave apāre pāram icchanto hate śūre mahātmani
english: With that great-souled hero slain, they were like merchants whose ship has broken apart upon a bottomless, boatless, shoreless sea, longing for the farther bank.

sanskrit: madrarāje mahārāja vitrastāḥ śaravikṣatāḥ anāthā nātham icchanto mṛgāḥ siṃhārditā iva
english: When the king of the Madras fell, O great king, terrified and torn by arrows, defenseless and longing for a protector, they were like deer harried by a lion.

sanskrit: vṛṣā yathā bhagnaśṛṅgāḥ śīrṇadantā gajā iva madhyāhne pratyapāyāma nirjitā dharmasūnunā
english: Like bulls with broken horns, like elephants with shattered tusks, at midday we withdrew, vanquished by the son of Dharma.

sanskrit: na saṃdhātum anīkāni na ca rājan parākrame āsīd buddhir hate śalye tava yodhasya kasya cit
english: When Śalya was slain, O king, not one of your warriors had the mind either to rally the ranks or to display valor.

sanskrit: bhīṣme droṇe ca nihate sūtaputre ca bhārata yad duḥkhaṃ tava yodhānāṃ bhayaṃ cāsīd viśāṃ pate tad bhayaṃ sa ca naḥ śoko bhūya evābhyavartata
english: O Bhārata, the grief and the fear that came upon your warriors when Bhīṣma and Droṇa and the son of the sūta were slain, O lord of peoples — that fear and that sorrow now returned upon us even more greatly.

sanskrit: nirāśāś ca jaye tasmin hate śalye mahārathe hatapravīrā vidhvastā vikṛttāś ca śitaiḥ śaraiḥ madrarāje hate rājan yodhās te prādravan bhayāt
english: Despairing now of victory, with Śalya the great chariot-warrior slain, their champions dead, scattered and gashed by sharp arrows — when the king of the Madras fell, O king, your warriors fled in fear.

sanskrit: aśvān anye gajān anye rathān anye mahārathāḥ āruhya javasaṃpannāḥ pādātāḥ prādravan bhayāt
english: Some mounting horses, some elephants, some chariots, those great warriors, and the foot-soldiers too, swift of foot, fled in fear.

sanskrit: dvisāhasrāś ca mātaṅgā girirūpāḥ prahāriṇaḥ saṃprādravan hate śalye aṅkuśāṅguṣṭhacoditāḥ
english: And two thousand war-elephants, mountainous and battle-ready, fled together when Śalya fell, goaded by the hook and the thumb.

sanskrit: te raṇād bharataśreṣṭha tāvakāḥ prādravan diśaḥ dhāvantaś cāpy adṛśyanta śvasamānāḥ śarāturāḥ
english: O best of the Bharatas, your men fled from the battlefield in every direction, and even as they ran they were seen gasping, tormented by arrows.

sanskrit: tān prabhagnān drutān dṛṣṭvā hatotsāhān parājitān abhyadravanta pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavāś ca jayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Seeing them broken, fleeing, their spirit gone, defeated, the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas, eager for victory, rushed upon them.

sanskrit: bāṇaśabdaravaś cāpi siṃhanādaś ca puṣkalaḥ śaṅkhaśabdaś ca śūrāṇāṃ dāruṇaḥ samapadyata
english: And there arose a fearsome din — the twang and whistle of arrows, abundant lion-roars, and the blare of the conches of the heroes.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu kauravaṃ sainyaṃ bhayatrastaṃ pravidrutam anyonyaṃ samabhāṣanta pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: Seeing the Kaurava army fear-stricken and fleeing in all directions, the Pāñcālas, together with the Pāṇḍavas, spoke to one another.

sanskrit: adya rājā satyadhṛtir jitāmitro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ adya duryodhano hīno dīptayā nṛpatiśriyā
english: Today King Yudhiṣṭhira, steadfast in truth, has conquered his foes; today Duryodhana is stripped of his blazing royal splendor.

sanskrit: adya śrutvā hataṃ putraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ niḥsaṃjñaḥ patito bhūmau kilbiṣaṃ pratipadyatām
english: Today, hearing that his son is slain, may King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, fall senseless to the ground and reap the fruit of his sin.

sanskrit: adya jānātu kaunteyaṃ samarthaṃ sarvadhanvinām adyātmānaṃ ca durmedhā garhayiṣyati pāpakṛt adya kṣattur vacaḥ satyaṃ smaratāṃ bruvato hitam
english: Today let him know the son of Kuntī to be the equal of all bowmen; today that evil-minded doer of wrong shall reproach himself; today let him remember the true and salutary words once spoken by Vidura.

sanskrit: adyaprabhṛti pārthāṃś ca preṣyabhūta upācaran vijānātu nṛpo duḥkhaṃ yat prāptaṃ pāṇḍunandanaiḥ
english: From this day, reduced to a servant and waiting upon the sons of Pṛthā, let the king know the sorrow that has befallen the joys of Pāṇḍu's sons.

sanskrit: adya kṛṣṇasya māhātmyaṃ jānātu sa mahīpatiḥ adyārjunadhanurghoṣaṃ ghoraṃ jānātu saṃyuge
english: Today let that lord of the earth know the greatness of Kṛṣṇa; today let him know the dread thunder of Arjuna's bow in battle.

sanskrit: astrāṇāṃ ca balaṃ sarvaṃ bāhvoś ca balam āhave adya jñāsyati bhīmasya balaṃ ghoraṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Today he shall know in battle the full power of his weapons and the strength of his arms — the terrible might of the great-souled Bhīma.

sanskrit: hate duryodhane yuddhe śakreṇevāsure maye yat kṛtaṃ bhīmasenena duḥśāsanavadhe tadā nānyaḥ kartāsti loke tad ṛte bhīmaṃ mahābalam
english: When Duryodhana is slain in battle — as the demon Maya was slain by Śakra — that deed which Bhīmasena wrought in the killing of Duḥśāsana, no other in the world but Bhīma of mighty strength could have done.

sanskrit: jānītām adya jyeṣṭhasya pāṇḍavasya parākramam madrarājaṃ hataṃ śrutvā devair api suduḥsaham
english: Today let them know the valor of the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas, hearing that the king of the Madras — hard to withstand even for the gods — has been slain.

sanskrit: adya jñāsyati saṃgrāme mādrīputrau mahābalau nihate saubale śūre gāndhāreṣu ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Today he shall know in battle the two mighty sons of Mādrī, when the valiant son of Subala is slain and the Gāndhāras are slaughtered to the last.

sanskrit: kathaṃ teṣāṃ jayo na syād yeṣāṃ yoddhā dhanaṃjayaḥ sātyakir bhīmasenaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ
english: How could victory not be theirs, whose warriors are Dhanaṃjaya, Sātyaki, Bhīmasena, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the grandson of Pṛṣata?

sanskrit: draupadyās tanayāḥ pañca mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau śikhaṇḍī ca maheṣvāso rājā caiva yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: The five sons of Draupadī, the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī, Śikhaṇḍin the great archer, and King Yudhiṣṭhira himself —

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ ca jagatāṃ nātho nāthaḥ kṛṣṇo janārdanaḥ kathaṃ teṣāṃ jayo na syād yeṣāṃ dharmo vyapāśrayaḥ
english: and whose protector is Kṛṣṇa Janārdana, the lord of the worlds — how could victory not be theirs, whose refuge is righteousness?

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ droṇaṃ ca karṇaṃ ca madrarājānam eva ca tathānyān nṛpatīn vīrāñ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Bhīṣma and Droṇa and Karṇa, and the king of the Madras too, and other heroic kings besides, by the hundreds and the thousands —

sanskrit: ko 'nyaḥ śakto raṇe jetum ṛte pārthaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram yasya nātho hṛṣīkeśaḥ sadā dharmayaśonidhiḥ
english: who else but Pṛthā's son Yudhiṣṭhira could vanquish them in battle, he whose protector is Hṛṣīkeśa, the everlasting treasury of righteousness and fame?

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vadamānās te harṣeṇa mahatā yutāḥ prabhagnāṃs tāvakān rājan sṛñjayāḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nvayuḥ
english: Speaking thus and filled with great joy, the Sṛñjayas, O king, pursued your broken men from behind.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayo rathānīkam abhyavartata vīryavān mādrīputrau ca śakuniṃ sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ
english: The valiant Dhanaṃjaya bore down upon the chariot-host, while the two sons of Mādrī and Sātyaki the great chariot-warrior fell upon Śakuni.

sanskrit: tān prekṣya dravataḥ sarvān bhīmasenabhayārditān duryodhanas tadā sūtam abravīd utsmayann iva
english: Beholding them all fleeing, tormented by fear of Bhīmasena, Duryodhana then spoke to his charioteer, smiling as it were.

sanskrit: na mātikramate pārtho dhanuṣpāṇim avasthitam jaghane sarvasainyānāṃ mamāśvān pratipādaya
english: "The son of Pṛthā shall not pass beyond me while I stand bow in hand. Drive my horses to the rear of all the troops."

sanskrit: jaghane yudhyamānaṃ hi kaunteyo māṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ notsahetābhyatikrāntuṃ velām iva mahodadhiḥ
english: "With me fighting at the rear, Dhanaṃjaya the son of Kuntī shall no more dare to pass beyond me than the great ocean dares overstep its shore."

sanskrit: paśya sainyaṃ mahat sūta pāṇḍavaiḥ samabhidrutam sainyareṇuṃ samuddhūtaṃ paśyasvainaṃ samantataḥ
english: "Behold, O charioteer, the great army overrun by the Pāṇḍavas; look upon the dust of the host raised up on every side."

sanskrit: siṃhanādāṃś ca bahuśaḥ śṛṇu ghorān bhayānakān tasmād yāhi śanaiḥ sūta jaghanaṃ paripālaya
english: "Hear the many lion-roars, dreadful and terrifying. Therefore go slowly, O charioteer, and guard the rear."

sanskrit: mayi sthite ca samare niruddheṣu ca pāṇḍuṣu punarāvartate tūrṇaṃ māmakaṃ balam ojasā
english: "With me standing firm in battle and the Pāṇḍavas held in check, my host will swiftly rally and return in full force."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā tava putrasya śūrāgryasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ sārathir hemasaṃchannāñ śanair aśvān acodayat
english: Hearing those words of your son, worthy of a foremost hero, the charioteer gently urged on the horses adorned with gold.

sanskrit: gajāśvarathibhir hīnās tyaktātmānaḥ padātayaḥ ekaviṃśatisāhasrāḥ saṃyugāyāvatasthire
english: Bereft of elephants, horses, and chariots, having forsaken all care for their lives, twenty-one thousand foot-soldiers stood ready for battle.

sanskrit: nānādeśasamudbhūtā nānārañjitavāsasaḥ avasthitās tadā yodhāḥ prārthayanto mahad yaśaḥ
english: Sprung from many lands, clad in garments of many hues, those warriors took their stand, seeking great glory.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ tatra saṃhṛṣṭānāṃ parasparam saṃmardaḥ sumahāñ jajñe ghorarūpo bhayānakaḥ
english: As they rushed upon one another there, exultant, a mighty clash arose, dreadful of form and terrifying.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ tadā rājan dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam balena caturaṅgeṇa nānādeśyā nyavārayan
english: Then, O king, men of many lands held back Bhīmasena and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the grandson of Pṛṣata with a fourfold force.

sanskrit: bhīmam evābhyavartanta raṇe 'nye tu padātayaḥ prakṣveḍyāsphoṭya saṃhṛṣṭā vīralokaṃ yiyāsavaḥ
english: But other foot-soldiers bore down upon Bhīma alone in battle — roaring and slapping their arms, exultant, eager to attain the world of heroes.

sanskrit: āsādya bhīmasenaṃ tu saṃrabdhā yuddhadurmadāḥ dhārtarāṣṭrā vinedur hi nānyāṃ cākathayan kathām parivārya raṇe bhīmaṃ nijaghnus te samantataḥ
english: Falling upon Bhīmasena, furious and maddened with the lust of battle, the followers of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son roared aloud and spoke of nothing else; surrounding Bhīma in the fray, they struck at him from every side.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānaḥ samare padātigaṇasaṃvṛtaḥ na cacāla rathopasthe maināka iva parvataḥ
english: Though assailed in battle, hemmed in by the throng of foot-soldiers, he did not stir from his chariot-seat, like Maināka the mountain.

sanskrit: te tu kruddhā mahārāja pāṇḍavasya mahāratham nigrahītuṃ pracakrur hi yodhāṃś cānyān avārayan
english: Enraged, O great king, they set themselves to seize that great chariot-warrior of the Pāṇḍavas, and held off the other warriors.

sanskrit: akrudhyata raṇe bhīmas tais tadā paryavasthitaiḥ so 'vatīrya rathāt tūrṇaṃ padātiḥ samavasthitaḥ
english: Bhīma grew wrathful in battle at those who beset him; quickly descending from his chariot, he took his stand on foot.

sanskrit: jātarūpaparicchannāṃ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām avadhīt tāvakān yodhān daṇḍapāṇir ivāntakaḥ
english: Grasping his great mace plated with gold, he slew your warriors like Death with his staff in hand.

sanskrit: rathāśvadvipahīnāṃs tu tān bhīmo gadayā balī ekaviṃśatisāhasrān padātīn avapothayat
english: Mighty Bhīma, with his mace, crushed those twenty-one thousand foot-soldiers, bereft of chariots, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit: hatvā tat puruṣānīkaṃ bhīmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ puraskṛtya nacirāt pratyadṛśyata
english: Having destroyed that host of men, Bhīma of true valor, placing Dhṛṣṭadyumna before him, soon came again into view.

sanskrit: pādātā nihatā bhūmau śiśyire rudhirokṣitāḥ saṃbhagnā iva vātena karṇikārāḥ supuṣpitāḥ
english: The slain foot-soldiers lay upon the ground, drenched in blood, like karṇikāra trees in full bloom broken down by the wind.

sanskrit: nānāpuṣpasrajopetā nānākuṇḍaladhāriṇaḥ nānājātyā hatās tatra nānādeśasamāgatāḥ
english: Wearing garlands of varied flowers and earrings of varied kinds, of varied birth and gathered from varied lands, they lay there slain.

sanskrit: patākādhvajasaṃchannaṃ padātīnāṃ mahad balam nikṛttaṃ vibabhau tatra ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam
english: That great host of foot-soldiers, covered with banners and standards, cut down, appeared there dreadful of aspect and terrifying.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirapurogās tu sarvasainyamahārathāḥ abhyadhāvan mahātmānaṃ putraṃ duryodhanaṃ tava
english: Then, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head, the great chariot-warriors of the whole army charged against your great-souled son Duryodhana.

sanskrit: te sarve tāvakān dṛṣṭvā maheṣvāsān parāṅmukhān nābhyavartanta te putraṃ veleva makarālayam
english: But all of them, seeing your great archers turned away in flight, did not press upon your son, as the shore does not encroach upon the abode of sea-monsters.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam apaśyāma tava putrasya pauruṣam yad ekaṃ sahitāḥ pārthā na śekur ativartitum
english: We beheld that marvel — the manhood of your son — that the sons of Pṛthā united could not overpass him, one though he was.

sanskrit: nātidūrāpayātaṃ tu kṛtabuddhiṃ palāyane duryodhanaḥ svakaṃ sainyam abravīd bhṛśavikṣatam
english: Duryodhana then spoke to his own army — sorely wounded, fled not far off, and bent upon flight —

sanskrit: na taṃ deśaṃ prapaśyāmi pṛthivyāṃ parvateṣu vā yatra yātān na vo hanyuḥ pāṇḍavāḥ kiṃ sṛtena vaḥ
english: "I see no place on earth or among the mountains where the Pāṇḍavas would not slay you once you fled there. What use is flight to you?"

sanskrit: alpaṃ ca balam eteṣāṃ kṛṣṇau ca bhṛśavikṣatau yadi sarve 'tra tiṣṭhāmo dhruvo no vijayo bhavet
english: "Small is their force, and the two Kṛṣṇas are sorely wounded. If we all stand firm here, our victory is assured."

sanskrit: viprayātāṃs tu vo bhinnān pāṇḍavāḥ kṛtakilbiṣān anusṛtya haniṣyanti śreyo naḥ samare sthitam
english: "But if you flee, scattered and guilty of wrong, the Pāṇḍavas will follow and slay you. Better for us to stand firm in battle."

sanskrit: śṛṇudhvaṃ kṣatriyāḥ sarve yāvantaḥ stha samāgatāḥ yadā śūraṃ ca bhīruṃ ca mārayaty antakaḥ sadā ko nu mūḍho na yudhyeta puruṣaḥ kṣatriyabruvaḥ
english: "Hear me, all you Kṣatriyas, as many as are gathered here: since Death ever slays alike the brave and the coward, what fool of a man who calls himself a Kṣatriya would not fight?"

sanskrit: śreyo no bhīmasenasya kruddhasya pramukhe sthitam sukhaḥ sāṃgrāmiko mṛtyuḥ kṣatradharmeṇa yudhyatām jitveha sukham āpnoti hataḥ pretya mahat phalam
english: "It is better for us to stand before the wrathful Bhīmasena. Death in battle is a blessing for those who fight by the law of the Kṣatriya: victorious, one wins happiness here; slain, one wins a great reward hereafter."

sanskrit: na yuddhadharmāc chreyān vai panthāḥ svargasya kauravāḥ acireṇa jitāṃl lokān hato yuddhe samaśnute
english: "There is no path to heaven better than the law of battle, O Kauravas. Slain in war, a man soon attains the worlds he has won."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya pūjayitvā ca pārthivāḥ punar evānvavartanta pāṇḍavān ātatāyinaḥ
english: Hearing his words and honoring them, the kings once more, with bows drawn to slay, turned upon the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tān āpatata evāśu vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ pratyudyayus tadā pārthā jayagṛdhrāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: As those striking warriors swiftly fell upon them in arrayed ranks, the striking sons of Pṛthā, greedy for victory, then went forth to meet them.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayo rathenājāv abhyavartata vīryavān viśrutaṃ triṣu lokeṣu gāṇḍīvaṃ vikṣipan dhanuḥ
english: The valiant Dhanaṃjaya advanced into the fray upon his chariot, drawing wide the bow Gāṇḍīva, renowned throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau ca śakuniṃ sātyakiś ca mahābalaḥ javenābhyapatan hṛṣṭā yato vai tāvakaṃ balam
english: And the two sons of Mādrī and the mighty Sātyaki, exultant, swiftly fell upon Śakuni, there where your host stood.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saṃnivṛtte balaughe tu śālvo mlecchagaṇādhipaḥ abhyavartata saṃkruddhaḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ sumahad balam
english: Saṃjaya said: When the flood of the host had turned back, Śālva, lord of the throngs of Mlecchas, in great fury advanced upon the very great army of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: āsthāya sumahānāgaṃ prabhinnaṃ parvatopamam dṛptam airāvataprakhyam amitragaṇamardanam
english: Mounted upon a mighty elephant in rut, like a mountain, proud, resembling Airāvata, a crusher of throngs of foes —

sanskrit: yo 'sau mahābhadrakulaprasūtaḥ; supūjito dhārtarāṣṭreṇa nityam sukalpitaḥ śāstraviniścayajñaiḥ; sadopavāhyaḥ samareṣu rājan
english: that elephant sprung of a great and noble breed, ever honored by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, well caparisoned by those skilled in the rules of the science, and always ridden into battle, O king —

sanskrit: tam āsthito rājavaro babhūva; yathodayasthaḥ savitā kṣapānte sa tena nāgapravareṇa rājann; abhyudyayau pāṇḍusutān samantāt śitaiḥ pṛṣatkair vidadāra cāpi; mahendravajrapratimaiḥ sughoraiḥ
english: Mounted upon it, that foremost of kings shone like the sun risen at the dawning. Upon that excellent elephant, O king, he advanced against the sons of Pāṇḍu on every side, and tore through them with sharp, dreadful arrows that were like the thunderbolt of great Indra.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarān vai sṛjato mahāraṇe; yodhāṃś ca rājan nayato yamāya nāsyāntaraṃ dadṛśuḥ sve pare vā; yathā purā vajradharasya daityāḥ
english: As he loosed his arrows in that great battle, O king, and led warriors to Yama, neither friend nor foe could find a chink in him — as of old the Daityas could find none in the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: te pāṇḍavāḥ somakāḥ sṛñjayāś ca; tam eva nāgaṃ dadṛśuḥ samantāt sahasraśo vai vicarantam ekaṃ; yathā mahendrasya gajaṃ samīpe
english: The Pāṇḍavas, the Somakas, and the Sṛñjayas saw that single elephant on every side, ranging as though it were a thousand, like the elephant of great Indra close at hand.

sanskrit: saṃdrāvyamāṇaṃ tu balaṃ pareṣāṃ; parītakalpaṃ vibabhau samantāt naivāvatasthe samare bhṛśaṃ bhayād; vimardamānaṃ tu parasparaṃ tadā
english: The army of the foe, driven in rout, appeared on every side as if encircled; in their great fear it stood no longer firm in battle, but trampled one upon another.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhagnā sahasā mahācamūḥ; sā pāṇḍavī tena narādhipena diśaś catasraḥ sahasā pradhāvitā; gajendravegaṃ tam apārayantī
english: Then that great Pāṇḍava host, suddenly broken by that lord of men, fled at once to the four quarters, unable to withstand the onset of that lord of elephants.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ vegavatā prabhagnāṃ; sarve tvadīyā yudhi yodhamukhyāḥ apūjayaṃs tatra narādhipaṃ taṃ; dadhmuś ca śaṅkhāñ śaśisaṃnikāśān
english: And seeing it broken by that swift charge, all your foremost warriors in the battle there honored that lord of men, and blew their conches white as the moon.

sanskrit: śrutvā ninādaṃ tv atha kauravāṇāṃ; harṣād vimuktaṃ saha śaṅkhaśabdaiḥ senāpatiḥ pāṇḍavasṛñjayānāṃ; pāñcālaputro na mamarṣa roṣāt
english: Then, hearing the shout of the Kauravas let loose in joy together with the blare of conches, the commander of the Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas, the son of Pāñcāla, could not endure it for wrath.

sanskrit: tatas tu taṃ vai dviradaṃ mahātmā; pratyudyayau tvaramāṇo jayāya jambho yathā śakrasamāgame vai; nāgendram airāvaṇam indravāhyam
english: Then that great-souled one, hastening for victory, went forth to meet that elephant, as Jambha of old, in his clash with Śakra, met Airāvaṇa, lord of elephants, the mount of Indra.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā tu dṛṣṭvā; pāñcālarājaṃ yudhi rājasiṃhaḥ taṃ vai dvipaṃ preṣayām āsa tūrṇaṃ; vadhāya rājan drupadātmajasya
english: Seeing the king of the Pāñcālas suddenly rushing upon him in battle, that lion among kings swiftly sent forth that elephant, O king, to slay the son of Drupada.
